name: Audit History
tagline: A record's audit history on the form: who changed what, when, and the old value beside the new — and a Restore to put it back.

limitations: The history comes from the preset's Sample data, not from Dataverse. On a form the control reads the history a page at a time through a same-origin call to the organisation's RetrieveRecordChangeHistory function — who, when and the old and new values in one answer — and there is no environment behind this origin to answer — so every preset carries a JSON history in the sampleData property and the control renders that. Opening a row, the column filter, Only this column and Load more all work against the same document.

A Restore on the demo writes into the preset's sample rather than to a record: the value goes back in the document and the restore appears as the newest row, by you — the same two things a form shows, without the confirmation dialog the platform would open first. On a form the write is webAPI.updateRecord on the record, behind openConfirmDialog, and the form is told it is behind until refreshed.
The empty-state sentences for auditing switched off come from the preset's auditing flags. On a form they come from the organisation row and the table's definition.

The values are the preset's own strings. On a form they are the platform's formatted values — a currency with its symbol, a choice as its label, a lookup as the related record's name — and the date is in the user's own time zone and locale.

Everything that never leaves the browser is real: the rows, the values table with old beside new, a cleared column, the 5 KB note, a share and a relationship as their own kinds, the filter, the scope chip, paging, the narrow layout, dark, RTL, and the hidden and no-access states.

presets.name: A record with a history
presets.description: Fourteen changes on an account: a lookup set, a column cleared, a choice changed, a value cut at the cap, a status change, an assignment, a share, a relationship, and the Create at the bottom.
